title: Equipment Installation Visits Charged to TimeBank Prepaid Service Hours
content:
For every installation visit drawn from a TimeBank Prepaid Service Hours block, and only for an installation visit, the minutes drawn and the block hours are figured under the installation pricing; a service visit, a remote session, a project time line and a travel entry keep their own minutes rules and are figured under their own schedules, and every other draw keeps the standard conversion.

A ticket's onsite labor is drawn once, when the service desk resolves the ticket, as one onsite-support draw dated the resolution's date for the minutes the resolution records.

**Band recorded.** For an installation visit the band is read from the service desk's resolution of the visit's ticket: holiday when the resolution falls on a Saturday or Sunday, after-hours for a weekday visit the desk resolved in the onsite after-hours class, and business hours otherwise, an installation being scheduled work and never an emergency, and a weekday observed holiday taking the band the resolution's class gives. Every other draw that is not a service visit, a remote session, a project time line or a travel entry keeps the standard time band.

The draw lowers the block's remaining hours and appears on the block's hours statement.

## Drawing an installation visit: `post_install_visit_draw_14ae60a8`

**Capability.** Draws the block hours of one onsite installation visit from a TimeBank block: one onsite-support draw is added to the block's hours ledger for the given service desk ticket and visit date, and the block's remaining hours go down by the hours drawn. The client sees the visit on the block's hours statement and the lower remaining balance.

**How it is invoked.** An agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it.

| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `timebank_block_id` | Reference number of the TimeBank block the visit is drawn from, as returned by the TimeBank block lookup. |
| `ticket_number` | The service desk ticket the visit was made on, SB- followed by 7 digits, as shown on the ticket record. |
| `entry_date` | The date of the visit, YYYY-MM-DD, US Eastern calendar date. |
| `time_band` | The band the draw is recorded in: `business_hours` records a draw priced at a multiplier of one; `after_hours` records a draw priced at the block's after-hours multiplier; `emergency` records an emergency call-out priced with the block's emergency multiplier; `holiday` records weekend or holiday work priced at the block's holiday multiplier; `not_applicable` is never used for a work draw and is listed only because the ledger carries it for other entries. |
| `resource_level` | The level the visit is drawn at: `technician` records a draw at the technician ratio; `senior_engineer` records a draw at the senior engineer ratio; `architect` records a draw at the solutions architect ratio; `not_applicable` is never used for a work draw. |
| `worked_minutes` | The minutes the visit is drawn for, integer minutes. |
| `hours` | The block hours the visit draws, 2 decimal places, rounded half up before it is passed. |

**Return.** `ledger_entry_reference` (reference of the new draw), `block_reference` (the block drawn from), `ticket_number`, `entry_date`, `hours` and `hours_balance_after` (the block's remaining hours after the draw, 2 decimal places). The `ledger_entry_reference` confirms the draw.
